Risk Management Plan Executive Summary for Corteva Agriscience, Pittsburg Operations

Revision History:
September 2025  This resubmission revises the Risk Management Plan to reflect current operations at Corteva Agriscience, Pittsburg Operations following the shutdown of several manufacturing unit operations in early to mid-2025.

a) 520 Block Operations, Process ID 1000130929:
An inventory of Hydrogen chloride (anhydrous) [Hydrochloric acid] below the Federal threshold quantity continues to be reported under this process to represent a unit operation that is considered a covered process due to connection to an anhydrous hydrogen chloride supply header (per the interconnectivity rule).
The solvent recovery process unit operation has been removed from the current resubmission.  This unit has ceased operation and has been de-inventoried of materials.
A source stream of anhydrous HCl from the 660 Block has been removed from the HCl absorption unit operation.  The 660 Block has ceased operations and no longer produces anhydrous HCl for absorption.

b) 660 Block Operations, Process ID 1000153028:
A Process, B Process (Stages 1-5), and Chlorine Unloading unit operations have been removed from the current resubmission.  These units have ceased operation and have been de-inventoried of materials.
The TOX (Thermal Oxidizer) unit process operation has been removed from the current resubmission. The TOX unit has ceased operation and has been de-inventoried of materials. 
Note: The current inventory of chlorine is below the Federal threshold quantity of 2,500 lbs. but is reported under this process to represent a unit operation that is considered a covered process due to connection to chlorine process operated by a site tenant company.  Also, the chlorine inventory is above the CalARP threshold quantity of 100 lbs.

c) Site Logistics Operations, Process ID 1000153030:
Chlorine railcars have been eliminated from the site and are therefore being removed from the Site Logisti

cs inventory.

e) Alternative Release Scenarios Updates:
With the modifications listed in process operations above, the Alternative Release Scenarios for HCl (anhydrous) and chlorine have been removed since the inventories are below Federal threshold quantities.
The site Worst Case Scenario (HF) and Alternative Release Scenarios for HF and SO2 remain unchanged from previous re-submittal.


1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
Corteva Agriscience, Pittsburg Operations is strongly committed to employee, public, and environmental safety.  This commitment is demonstrated by Pittsburg Operations comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at Pittsburg Operations.  It is Pittsburg Operations' policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances.  Pittsburg Operations is also committed to responding to emergencies resulting from accidental releases in order to mitigate the release and any associated consequences.

2. The Stationary Source and the Regulated Substances Handled
Agricultural chemical manufacturing ceased at Pittsburg Operations in March 2025.  However, Corteva still provides utilities and services for industrial tenants.  Pittsburg Operations has two regulated substances present at the site in quantities above the Federal RMP threshold quantities.  These substances are hydrogen fluoride (anhydrous) and sulfur dioxide (anhydrous).  The site manages sulfur dioxide (anhydrous) railcars and hydrogen fluoride railcars for a site tenant that uses those chemicals to manufacture an agricultural product. 
Note: Three other regulated substances are handled at Pittsburg Operations but at quantities below the Federal RMP threshold quantities: anhydrous ammonia, chlorine, and hydrogen chloride (anhydrous).  Quantities of anhydrous ammonia and chlorine are above Ca

lARP threshold quantities and are therefore regulated under the CalARP Program.  Hydrogen chloride (anhydrous) and chlorine are considered covered processes because of interconnectivity with onsite tenant chemical processes.  
	Ammonia (anhydrous) is used in pollution control equipment for a boiler at Pittsburg Operations.  
	Pittsburg Operations owns the chlorine header pipeline that transports chlorine vapor from one tenant company to another.
	Pittsburg Operations receives hydrogen chloride (anhydrous) from an onsite tenant and processes it into aqueous hydrochloric acid (36% by weight) at the HCl absorption unit.

3. The General Accidental Release Prevention Program
Pittsburg Operations has taken all the necessary steps to comply with the accidental release prevention requirements set out under 40 CFR part 68 of the EPA.  Pittsburg Operations was designed and constructed in accordance with RAGAGEP.  The following sections briefly describe the elements of the release prevention program that is in place at the site.

Process Safety Information
Pittsburg Operations maintains detailed records of safety information that describe the chemical hazards, operating parameters and equipment designs associated with all processes. Examples include: Material Safety Data Sheets, piping and instrumentation diagrams, equipment specification sheets, reactive chemicals testing reports, and corrosion reports.  This information is regularly reviewed, as needed, and is readily accessible to plant operations personnel.

Process Hazard Analysis
Pittsburg Operations conducts comprehensive studies to ensure that hazards associated with the covered processes are identified and effectively controlled.  The methodology used to carry out these analyses include Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Layers of Protection Analysis (LOPA), Reactive Chemical/Process Hazard Analysis (RC/PHA), Reactive Chemical Reviews, and Project Safety & Loss Prevention Reviews.  Studies utilize an appropriate

team of qualified personnel with expertise in engineering, maintenance and process operations and are revalidated on a regular basis.  Any findings related to the hazard analysis, where a response is required, are tracked to ensure resolution in a timely and appropriate manner.

Operating Procedures
For the purposes of safely conducting activities within Pittsburg Operations' covered processes, written operating procedures are maintained.  These procedures address various modes of operation such as initial startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, emergency operations, normal shutdown and startup after a turnaround.  This information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to plant operations personnel.

Training
Pittsburg Operations has a comprehensive training program in place to ensure that employees who are operating processes are competent in the operating procedures and safe work practices associated with these processes.  Refresher training is provided at least once every 3 years, and more frequently as needed, for required process and safety topics.

Mechanical Integrity
Pittsburg Operations carries out documented maintenance checks on process equipment to ensure safe and reliable operations.  Process equipment examined by these checks includes among others pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping systems, relief and vent systems, critical instruments, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and pumps. Qualified personnel with previous training in maintenance practices are utilized to carry out appropriate maintenance.  These personnel are also offered specialized training as needed.  Any equipment deficiencies identified by the maintenance checks are corrected in a safe and timely manner.

Management of Change
Written procedures are in place at Pittsburg Operations to safely manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures.  Process operators, maintenance personnel, or any other employee whose job

tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of and offered training to deal with the modification.

Pre-startup Reviews
Pre-start up safety reviews related to new processes and to modifications in established processes are conducted by appropriate personnel as a regular practice at Pittsburg Operations.  These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, and operating and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation.

Compliance Audits
Pittsburg Operations conducts self-assessments of the management systems designed to ensure RMP requirements on a regular basis.  These self-assessments are carried out at least once every 3 years by each facility.  Any corrective actions identified as a result of the self-assessments are tracked to ensure resolution in a timely and appropriate manner.

Incident Investigation
Pittsburg Operations promptly and carefully investigates any incident that has resulted in, or could reasonably result in, a catastrophic release of a regulated substance.  These investigations are undertaken to identify the situation leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent the release from reoccurring.  All reports are retained for a minimum of 5 years.

Employee Participation
Pittsburg Operations truly believes that process safety management and accident prevention is a team effort.  Company employees are strongly encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements.  Element-specific employee surveys or management system reviews are conducted quarterly, and the results are summarized and shared with all site personnel. In addition, Pittsburg Operations employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP rule, including information resulting from process hazard analyses in particular. Safe job performance is required for each of th

e jobs at the site.

Contractors
Pittsburg Operations hires contractors to conduct specialized maintenance, construction, and various other activities.  Prior to selecting a contractor, a thorough evaluation of safety performance of the contractor is carried out.  Pittsburg Operations has a policy of informing the contractors of known potential hazards related to the contractor's work and the processes. Contractors are also required to inform Pittsburg Operations of any hazards they may introduce at the site. Contractors are also informed of all the procedures for emergency response should an accidental release of a regulated substance occur.

4. Five-year Accident History
Pittsburg Operations has an excellent record of preventing accidental releases due to the site's release prevention policies.  There is only one accident on the sites five-year accident history.
On May 13th, 2021, a minor chlorine leak resulted in an injury (OSHA recordable) to a Corteva employee. Approximately three pounds of chlorine was released as the result of packing failure on one of the valves.  The injured employee was looking for the leak without wearing the appropriate PPE.  As a result of the incident, Operations was retrained on PPE requirements and new equipment was purchased to facilitate the identification of leak points. There were no offsite consequences.

5. Emergency Response Plan
Pittsburg Operations utilizes a written emergency response plan to deal with accidental releases of hazardous materials.  The plan includes all aspects of emergency response including adequate first aid and medical treatment, sheltering-in-place, notification of local emergency response agencies and the public, as well as post-incident decontamination of affected areas.  To ensure proper functioning, Pittsburg Operations emergency response equipment is regularly inspected and serviced.  In addition, the plan is promptly updated to reflect any pertinent changes taking place that would require a modifi

ed emergency response.

CA Region II LEPC is the Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) with which the emergency plan for the Pittsburg Operations site has been coordinated and verified. Pittsburg Operations also coordinates our plans and actions with local agencies and industrial mutual aid groups, which provide Pittsburg Operations with additional emergency response capability.

6. Planned Changes to Improve Safety
Improving safety is a continuous process at Pittsburg Operations.  PHA's, Compliance Audits, Technology Reviews, Facility Self-Assessments and Management System Reviews, Incident Investigations, Emergency Response Drills and employee participation are primary means for identifying opportunities to improve safety.  Structural seismic upgrades, materials of construction upgrades, installation of additional process instrumentation and/or process controls, and conducting Hazard Awareness training are typical of currently planned changes to improve safety at the facility.  As another example of Pittsburg Operations' commitment to continuous improvement in safety, the site was CalOSHA Voluntary Protection Plan (VPP) Star certified in 2013 and recertified in 2017, and 2023.

Additional information regarding process descriptions, Worst-Case and Alternative Release Scenario impact maps, public receptors, etc., is available at the Pittsburg Operations Site.
